I don't know how to read or write, but I've been farming these 8 mu in Quzhou for more than 40 years, and I know what works. I'm 60 now, and my wife and I still do most of the work ourselves — we can't afford to hire much help. This year, I'll put 6 mu into wheat and maize like always. That's the backbone of our food and income. After we cut the wheat in early June, we plant the maize right away, sometimes the very next day; there's no time to waste between crops. I'll keep 2 mu in cotton too. Cotton is hard on the back with all the picking, but the price has been steady and my wife is still good at it.

For the wheat, I'll rotary till the soil in early October before sowing. I use the improved lumai seed — about 30 jin per mu, same as my neighbor and same as last year. At planting, I put down one big bag of compound fertilizer per mu, the 15-15-15 kind, about 50 kg. Then when the wheat starts jointing in spring, I spread about 20 jin of urea on top. I irrigate three times: once after planting if the autumn is dry, once at jointing, and once when the grain is filling. Water costs more every year, so three times is what I can afford. For sprays, I do herbicide once, insecticide twice, and fungicide once — four times total. I expect about 800 kg per mu if the weather treats us right.

For the maize, I plant the Denghai 605 hybrid — one package per mu — right after the wheat comes off in mid-June. There's no time for ploughing, so we no-till plant it. I put down about 40 kg of that high-nitrogen compound, the 28-6-6 type. Maize needs water at the trumpet stage and maybe once more in August if it's dry, so twice total. I spray for insects twice and weeds once.

For cotton, I rotary till in April and plant the local improved variety. I use about 50 kg of compound fertilizer per mu at planting, and topdress again later when the plants are flowering. Cotton needs more sprays because of the bollworms — about five times total between herbicide, insecticide, and growth regulator. I irrigate twice, before flowering and during the boll stage.

I expect about 800 kg per mu for wheat, 950 kg per mu for maize, and 250 kg per mu of cotton lint. My yields have been close to this in normal years. I don't take big risks — I do what my father did, what my neighbors do, and what the land has always given us.
